classification.difficultyReason: Convert constant deceleration into table speeds, plot the supplied time intervals, then interpret the triangular area as distance; the parts scaffold this routine sequence.

content.prompt: A cyclist travelling at $6\text{ m/s}$ applies the brakes and decelerates at a constant rate of $2\text{ m/s}^2$.

inlines.text: . The missing speeds, from left to right, are

children.label: b
children.prompt: Plot a speed-time graph for the 3 seconds shown in the table above.

answer.short: A straight line from $(0,6)$ to $(3,0)$, with time in seconds and speed in metres per second.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5 supplied graph beneath parts b and c
spec.description: Complete answer graph with a straight speed-time segment, neutral grey grid, black axes and blue series. Source blue axes and grid use house graph styling.
spec.mathematics: Speed decreases linearly from 6 m/s at 0 s to 0 m/s at 3 s. Grid increments are 0.25 s horizontally and 1 m/s vertically; grid extends to 3.25 s and 8 m/s.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Calculate the distance travelled during the 3 seconds of deceleration.

answer.worked:
The distance travelled is the triangular area under the speed-time graph.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance}&=\frac12\times3\times6\\&=9\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
